subject: English
title: CISCE curriculum: English, Class VI

source.read: A third-party copy of the Class VI pages of the CISCE curriculum (English: printed pages 1 to 15), hosted by BYJU'S
source.note: UNOFFICIAL SOURCE. The pages do not name their publisher or year, and were read through a text summary of the PDF, not the PDF itself. The official document on cisce.org could not be reached from the build environment. CISCE is understood not to prescribe a textbook for this class, so a school's own book and term plan may order or extend these topics.

licence: Strand names as printed (facts). Every outcome is written by OpenPath in its own words with a pointer to its strand and line; no curriculum text is reproduced.
review: OpenPath curriculum inventory (research from a secondary source; not an educator review)

outcomes.text: Answers questions on a passage heard or read.
outcomes.note: Listen and answer for passages heard; the Reading course for passages read.

outcomes.text: Follows the issues in spoken texts and asks for things to be made clear.
outcomes.note: Listen and answer checks that a spoken passage is followed; asking for things to be made clear is not practised.

outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Understands texts, draws conclusions and reads between the lines.
outcomes.note: Reading covers cause and effect and how characters feel; wider inference is not a separate skill yet.

outcomes.text: Separates the main points from personal opinions or judgements.
outcomes.note: Reading course: fact and opinion.

outcomes.text: Works out what words and phrases mean, including figurative and suggested meanings.
Reads graded literature: stories, plays, poems, travel writing, life stories, reports, speeches and articles.
outcomes.note: The suggested books are published works and are not in the app. The learner reads one and tells a grown-up about it; the app's own stories are in Reading.

outcomes.text: Applies the basic rules of grammar and usage in speaking and writing.
outcomes.note: Grammar in use, at the learner's level.

outcomes.text: Uses pronouns in the right form, and reflexive pronouns correctly.
Notices wrong changes in a pronoun's number or person.
Varies sentence patterns for meaning and style.
Uses the words around a word or phrase to work out its meaning.
Uses common prefixes, suffixes and roots as clues to meaning.
Uses print and digital references for how a word is said, what it means and its part of speech.
outcomes.note: Done with a grown-up, away from the app, who ticks what they saw.

outcomes.text: Understands figures of speech where they are used.
Makes subject and verb agree when a phrase or clause comes between them.
Tells transitive verbs from intransitive ones.
Makes pronouns agree with the nouns they stand for, including words like each and everyone.
outcomes.note: Matching a pronoun to its noun is practised; words like each and everyone are not yet.

outcomes.text: Keeps verb tenses steady across paragraphs.
outcomes.note: Practised within a sentence, not across a paragraph.

outcomes.text: Spells frequently used words correctly.
outcomes.note: The Spelling Bee, and words misspelt in writing that return as My tricky words.

outcomes.text: Forms and uses the perfect tenses.
Notices wrong changes of tense.
